newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Peacekeeper guarding election site dies in shooting.
newsitem.headline: Peacekeeper guarding election site dies in shooting.

text.p: A soldier in Bosnia's NATO-led peace force died of a gunshot wound on Sunday while guarding a Sarajevo warehouse filled with voting materials for next weekend's general elections, international officials said.

Initial reports said the Ukrainian peacekeeper appeared to have been shot by an intruder outside the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe building, but NATO said later an investigation found no evidence of this.
"We are prepared to say now that there was no involvement by former warring factions," Major Brett Boudreau of the peace Implementation Force (IFOR) in Bosnia said.
He declined to elaborate. But his account suggested the Ukrainian soldier might have been killed by an accidental or intentional discharge of his own gun.
Ukrainian sentries at the warehouse said a few hours after the incident that their comrade died inside an armoured personnel carrier where he was on duty.

The shooting occurred at 12.30 a.m. (2230 GMT) on Sunday and the Ukrainian was pronounced dead at a nearby IFOR hospital a half hour later. His identity was being withheld pending notification of his family.
The warehouse contains ballot papers and other materials for Bosnia's first postwar elections next Saturday supervised by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.
IFOR troops began guarding the building a week ago after heaps of election materials were stored there.
